Timeline::month_start_scalar¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

bool Timeline::month_start_scalar() const

Test The First Local Calendar Day¶

month_start_scalar() is true whenever the scalar instant’s local day of month is 1. Clock time does not need to be midnight: every instant occurring on the first local date satisfies the predicate.

This is a calendar-position query, not a test that the instant equals the month’s opening boundary. Use floor("D") if a midnight instant is required. Use is_month_start() for arrays.

Example: First Day Versus Last Day¶

const auto first = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-01T12:00:00Z");
const auto last = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:00:00Z");
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "Feb 1=" << first.month_start_scalar()
          << ", Feb 29=" << last.month_start_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

Feb 1=true, Feb 29=false

Example: Timezone Can Change The Date¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-04-01T01:00:00Z");
const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "UTC=" << utc.month_start_scalar()
          << ", Edmonton=" << local.month_start_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

UTC=true, Edmonton=false

Absence And Failure¶

NaT returns false. Any non-scalar shape throws, including shape [1]. Neither result mutates or rounds the receiver.

See Also¶

  • is_month_start(): shape-preserving predicate.

  • month_end_scalar(): test the month’s final date.

  • day_scalar(): read the day-of-month field directly.
